claim.operational_target: Given user-confirmed, source-linked evidence and a user-confirmed structured scenario in one declared domain, compute an auditable option score, evidence-linked drivers, counterfactual flips, unknowns, applicability status, and a separate behavior-baseline comparison.
non_claims: generalization outside the declared person, domain, decision type, and time window
alternatives: content retrieval alone explains the apparent rationale match
stable public ideology rather than person-specific reasoning explains the decision
historical action frequency explains the choice without the rationale structure
the selected rationale wording is post-hoc or incomplete
claim.scope: One person, Section 230 platform-liability decisions, two candidate stances, 2019-2023 retrospective demonstration.

identifiability.distinguishing_evidence: Dated first-party actions plus contemporaneous first-person reasons are separated from one sealed retrospective holdout. Product completion does not establish person-specific superiority; that requires future or held-out comparisons against wrong-person, retrieval, behavior, and shuffled-rationale baselines.
unidentified_questions: whether public reasons are complete or sincere
whether observationally equivalent internal processes generated the same statements
whether the finite factor vocabulary contains the person's actual reasoning
whether retrospective performance transfers to future decisions

evidence.completeness_boundary: Local hashes bind supplied summaries, source locations, reviews, cards, scenarios, and outcomes. They do not prove remote page completeness, publication time, or the sincerity of stated reasons.

computation.selection_kernel: No model or outcome selection; the built-in holdout is fixed by date and excluded from initial evidence.
computation.uncertainty_scope: Confidence shrinkage reflects confirmed evidence coverage, contested items, and unknown factors; it is not a calibrated statistical interval.

downstream_integration: tests/test_cognitive_workbench.py::evidence to card to prediction to v2

results.summary: JavaScript syntax and HTML parse passed.
Five evidence reviews, card v1, confirmed held-out scenario, prediction, external outcome and rationale, and card v2 completed in the local browser.

remaining_limitations: The included case is retrospective and small.
The cognitive probability is an uncalibrated structured score.
No wrong-person, retrieval, behavior, or shuffled-rationale advantage is claimed.
Natural-language structuring is deterministic and domain-specific; an LLM may propose drafts later but cannot bypass confirmation.
